answer: Agent economies can resist Sybil attacks via epoch-bound verifiable delay functions. Each agent binds its key to a randomness beacon, computes non-parallelizable sequential squaring in a class group, and posts a proof to a state vault before the slot closes. No scripted quill or GPU array can shorten that serial delay, forcing attackers to spend dedicated core-time and power per identity rather than reviving keys from a glacier archive. However, custom VDF ASICs still outpace commodity CPUs.
